chapter_name: Long Writing Skills: Letters, Paragraphs, and Emails
learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to structure your thoughts to write brilliant paragraphs, polite formal letters, and modern digital emails!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A good paragraph is like a hamburger! The top bun is the 'Topic Sentence' (tells the main idea). The meat and veggies are the 'Supporting Sentences' (details, facts, and examples). The bottom bun is the 'Concluding Sentence' (wraps it up nicely).

main_concepts.concept_title: 👔 Formal Letters (To the Principal or Editor)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Formal letters are written to people in charge. You must be polite and direct. Format: Sender's Address -> Date -> Receiver's Address -> Subject (Very Important!) -> Salutation (Respected Sir/Madam) -> Body (3 short paragraphs) -> Closing (Yours faithfully/sincerely).

Informal letters are chatty and friendly! You do not need a Subject line or the receiver's address. You can ask about their health, share funny stories, and use emotional words. Close with 'Lots of love' or 'Yours affectionately'.

Emails are super fast digital letters. The layout has a 'To:' (email address), 'Cc:' (carbon copy), and a 'Subject:' box. The Subject must be catchy and short (e.g., 'Leave Application for 2 Days'). Keep the body brief, and always sign off with your name.
Never start writing immediately! Use CODER: C-Collect ideas, O-Organize them logically, D-Draft (write it down), E-Edit (check spelling and grammar), R-Rewrite the final perfect version!

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Hamburger Paragraph
fun_activity.instructions: Write a 5-sentence paragraph about 'My Favourite Superpower'. Remember the Hamburger rule! 1 Top Bun sentence, 3 Meat/Veggie detail sentences, and 1 Bottom Bun concluding sentence.

quick_recap: ⭐ Paragraphs need a clear Topic Sentence, supporting details, and a solid conclusion.
⭐ Formal letters require strict formatting (both addresses, a subject line, and formal tone).
⭐ Informal letters are friendly, relaxed, and skip the subject line and receiver's address.
⭐ Emails need a clear, specific Subject line so the reader knows exactly what it is about.
⭐ Always plan your points before you start writing long compositions!
